recipients.theme: oaths and the Troth; the danger of identifying the vow with the thing it was meant to serve
gift and identity; gift must pass through a wolf without becoming possession
mortality, diminishing strength, relinquishment, and the passage of keeping into other paws
Unclaimed Virtue; goodness performed through a wolf does not prove that the wolf possesses goodness
presence and withdrawal; when silence serves attention and when it becomes abandonment
courage without fearlessness; answering while fear remains
discernment and suspicion; when vigilance hardens and fear mistakes itself for sight
the fallen and their return; mercy without denial of wound or guilt
strength and guardianship; the fang may guard but cannot enthrone itself
grief and authority; the wound may teach but cannot crown
remaining without absolutizing preservation; the Troth may remain when structures do not

chiasm.correction: Do not become the thing entrusted to you.
What must actually remain when gifts, forms, traditions, and structures change?
Neither death nor suffering confers possession of virtue.
Neither goodness nor power becomes righteousness because a wolf bears it.
Keeping requires discerning when not to act and when another's cry cannot be left unanswered.
What do we fear, and what do we truly see?
